title: TEBench: a source-labelled thermoelectric data collection with leakage-safe splits and baselines for machine learning
description:
v1.0.1 of TEBench, corresponding to the ChemRxiv preprint (DOI 10.26434/chemrxiv.15011944). The manuscript has been submitted to ACS Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling and has not been accepted. v1.0.0 is archived as DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24151805.

Three source-labelled thermoelectric tables are kept separate: Starrydata Experiment-labelled curves, a JARVIS-DFT transport extract, and an audited bulk Bi2Te3 workbook. DFT and experimental targets are never pooled. This version includes the sample-level Starrydata harmonised table, Starrydata baseline and revision prediction files, canonical-composition keys, proposed leakage-safe paper/family/formula splits (seed 20261107), an eight-paper own-data hold-out, κ-only physical screening, and CPU reference and tuned baselines.

Code is released under the MIT License. Bundled data have mixed upstream licences; see NOTICE.md. Starrydata-derived files are redistributed under CC BY 4.0 with attribution to Katsura et al., STAM: Methods 5, 2506976 (2025) and to the original source-paper DOIs, and with an indication of the harmonisation, flags and predictions added here. Raw official ThermoelectricMaterials papers, samples and curves files, and intermediate long/point dumps, are not redistributed; rebuild them from the pinned snapshot (SHA-256 hashes in metrics/download_provenance.json).
